== proof/ConRon/Refine/Main.lean#L270-L291
   270  /-- info: 'ConRon.Refine.conron.no_proof_of_False'' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
   271  #guard_msgs in #print axioms conron.no_proof_of_False'
   272  
   273  /-! ## The headline: the pins the verified decoder produced (task #75)
   274  
   275  `hvar` is a promise about the pin *argument*, and the one place a real run gets
   276  it from is the decoder: `con_ron::driver::pins_for_run` calls
   277  `kernel::pins_decode::decode_embedded()`, and task #66's `PinsWF.decode_wf`
   278  reads `PinsWF` off **any** successful decode run — the input is a `Slice U8`
   279  like any other, and nothing about its value is used.  So the pair below is the
   280  statement about *the binary's checker fed the pins its own verified decoder
   281  produced*, with no hypothesis left but that decode and the run itself, and it
   282  names no string constant: its census is con-leche's own three axioms.
   283  
   284  The two `_embedded` corollaries in the next section are this pair's instance at
   285  `text = core.str.Str.as_bytes kernel.pins_text.PINS_TEXT` — `decode_embedded`
   286  is that `as_bytes` followed by `decode`, which is what `decode_embedded_wf`
   287  peels — and they pay one axiom for naming the constant (`AENEAS_FINDINGS.md`
   288  §3.8).  They are kept as they are: the extra generality here is exactly the
   289  step that drops the axiom, and both statements are worth having side by side. -/
   290  
   291  /-- **The main theorem for the shipped binary, axiom-free** (task #75): every

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L130-L254
   130  const USAGE: &str = "\
   131  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
   132                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
   133                 FILE.ndjson
   134         con-ron --help
   135  
   136    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   137                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   138                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists,
   139                      ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean), so a stream declaring a
   140                      theorem of type False is never accepted
   141                      (ConLeche.no_False_theorem_accepted).  What the port
   142                      proves is that same statement about THIS program's fold
   143                      (DESIGN.md §1); con-leche's file-level corollary
   144                      ConLeche.no_False_declaration, which covers the parse as
   145                      well, is NOT yet claimed here -- task #84 put the parser
   146                      into the verified core, so the corollary is now reachable,
   147                      but its proof is the next task's.
   148    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   149                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   150                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   151    --jobs=<n>        the check phase's worker count: <n> workers claim records
   152                      one at a time off a shared counter, and --jobs=1 runs the
   153                      plain loop with no counter and no result table.  The
   154                      verdict, and the declaration a rejection names, are the
   155                      same at every <n>: the results are walked in RECORD order,
   156                      so the first failing record in fold order is the one
   157                      reported.  Each worker reserves 1 GiB of address space for
   158                      its stack, so a run under `ulimit -v` needs 3x the
   159                      checker's resident set plus a gigabyte per worker; the
   160                      DEFAULT is one worker per hardware thread capped at 16 for
   161                      that reason (con-leche's uncapped default aborts on a
   162                      96-thread machine).  0 or a non-numeral is a usage error,
   163                      as in con-leche.
   164    --no-mark-persistent
   165                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP: the mark it turns off is a
   166                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   167                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this program's counts are
   168                      std::sync::Arc counts -- atomic by type, in every lane,
   169                      with no runtime mark to clear.  A run that passes it says
   170                      so on stderr.
   171    --progress[=<stride>]
   172                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   173                      phase:
   174                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   175                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   176                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> checks pending t=<s>s
   177                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   178                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   179                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s, <n> workers
   180                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   181                      declaration is installed (<i> is its FOLD position, which
   182                      the stream's record index sits near but not at a fixed
   183                      offset above), so a run that dies in the install phase
   184                      names the declaration it died in on its last line.  A
   185                      check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th COMPLETED
   186                      check.  On a failure the phase's closing line says so
   187                      ('install failed at', 'check failed at') and the summary
   188                      still prints.  Bare --progress is stride 1; a stride that
   189                      is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is a usage error.
   190    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   191                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   192                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.
   193    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   194                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   195                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   196                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   197                      verified core and decoded by it.
   198    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   199                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   200                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   201                      measurement can be reproduced.
   202  
   203  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   204  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   205  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   206  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   207  
   208  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   209  exits 3 without reading its input.
   210  
   211  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   212  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: con-leche's exit 1 for it is the Lean
   213  runtime's own panic, and this program instead aborts the way Rust aborts on a
   214  failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT, which a
   215  shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   216  
   217  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   218  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   219  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   220  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   221  declaration IS counted -- the preparation moves it to the front rather than
   222  dropping it, and it is what installs.  That count is a property of the INPUT.
   223  The number of environment CONSTANTS is not: an inductive record installs
   224  several constants (type former, constructors, recursor, projection table), so
   225  it moves when the representation moves.
   226  
   227  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   228  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   229  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   230  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   231  the export chose.  The stream's OWN copy of a prelude declaration is moved to
   232  the front in the prelude's order, and only the prelude records the stream does
   233  not declare are synthesised; a pinned operation's stream-certified structural
   234  ground (Nat.ble, Nat.sub, Nat.mul) is HOISTED ahead of the operation when the
   235  stream declares it later.  All of that is one pure total function from the
   236  file's records to the fold's input (con_ron::frontend::prepare); the parse
   237  itself only decodes, and recognising a block as a pinned basis block or a
   238  record as the quotient package's is the FOLD's.
   239  
   240  environment (con-leche's):
   241    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   242                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   243                                 declines it, having found no route
   244    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   245                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   246    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   247  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches and they go with it: no
   248  environment variable this program reads can shape a verdict, which is
   249  con-leche's own rule -- every such switch is a command-line flag.
   250  
   251  NOT PORTED: CON_LECHE_INMODEL_DUMP, the debug splice of the generated records
   252  into a copy of the input -- it is written through con-leche's annotated-NDJSON
   253  writer (`Frontend/ExportWrite.lean`), an output path this checker does not
   254  have.";

== scripts/setup-aeneas-lean.sh#L1-L14
     1  #!/usr/bin/env bash
     2  # Produce `_tmp/aeneas-lean/`: a copy of `vendor/aeneas/backends/lean` with
     3  # `patches/aeneas-433.patch` applied, so that the Aeneas Lean library
     4  # builds on con-leche's toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0 + Mathlib v4.33.0).
     5  # See DESIGN.md, task #2.
     6  #
     7  # Idempotent: a stamp records the patch's and the source tree's hashes; a
     8  # second run with nothing changed is a no-op and, crucially, keeps the
     9  # existing `.lake/` (rebuilding Mathlib's dependents costs minutes).
    10  #
    11  # Exits non-zero if the patch does not apply cleanly to the pinned Aeneas
    12  # submodule -- that is the signal that the submodule moved and the patch needs
    13  # rebasing.
    14  #

   430  pub fn mk_const(n: Name, us: Vec<Level>) -> Expr {
   431      let h: u64 = hash32(name::mix_hash(
   432          11,
   433          name::mix_hash(name::hash_data(&n), level::levels_hash(&us)),
   434      ));
   435      let d: u64 = pack_data(h, 0, 0, level::levels_have_param(&us));
   436      Expr(ptr::new(ExprNode { data: d, kind: ExprKind::Const(n, ptr::new(us)) }))
   437  }

  5086  pub fn whnf_core(
  5087      mode: &CheckMode,
  5088      fuel: u64,
  5089      st: &mut CState,
  5090      fe: &FEnv,
  5091      d: u64,
  5092      e: &Expr,
  5093  ) -> CheckM<Expr> {
  5094      const M: [u32; 24] = [
  5095          102, 117, 101, 108, 32, 101, 120, 104, 97, 117, 115, 116, 101, 100, 58, 32, 119, 104,
  5096          110, 102, 67, 111, 114, 101,
  5097      ];
  5098      if fuel == 0 {
  5099          Err(core_types::internal(core_types::code_points(&M)))
  5100      } else {
  5101          match whnf_core_probe(st, e) {
  5102              Some(r) => Ok(r),
  5103              None => match whnf_core_body_i(mode, fuel - 1, st, fe, d, e) {
  5104                  Err(err) => Err(err),
  5105                  Ok(r) => {
  5106                      st.whnf_core_c.insert(expr::dup(e), expr::dup(&r));
  5107                      Ok(r)
  5108                  }
  5109              },
  5110          }
  5111      }
  5112  }

  1328  pub fn decode(t: &[u8]) -> CheckM<Vec<NatOpPinSet>> {
  1329      let hdr = pins_header();
  1330      if !starts_with_from(t, &hdr, 0) {
  1331          Err(bad_text())
  1332      } else {
  1333          run_records(t, hdr.len(), tables_new())
  1334      }
  1335  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/cached/checker_c.rs#L123-L132
   123  pub fn or_else_step(attempt: CheckM<bool>) -> OrElseStep {
   124      match attempt {
   125          Ok(true) => OrElseStep::Matched,
   126          Ok(false) => OrElseStep::Continue,
   127          Err(e) => match e {
   128              CheckError::Native(m) => OrElseStep::Failed(CheckError::Native(m)),
   129              _ => OrElseStep::Recovered(e),
   130          },
   131      }
   132  }

== proof/ConRon/Refine/State.lean#L640-L671
   640  structure StateRel (st : cached.state_c.CState)
   641      (lst : ConLeche.Cached.CState) : Prop where
   642    ienv : HashMap.RelOn NameWF st.ienv lst.ienv absName absCConstE
   643    constTyAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_ty_at lst.constTyAt
   644      absNameLevels absExpr
   645    constValAt : HashMap.RelOn NameLevelsWF st.const_val_at lst.constValAt
   646      absNameLevels absExpr
   647    ruleRhsAt : HashMap.RelOn NameNameLevelsWF st.rule_rhs_at lst.ruleRhsAt
   648      absNameNameLevels absExpr
   649    whnfCoreC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_core_c lst.whnfCoreC absExpr absExpr
   650    whnfC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.whnf_c lst.whnfC absExpr absExpr
   651    inferC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_c lst.inferC absExpr absExpr
   652    inferIOC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.infer_io_c lst.inferIOC absExpr absExpr
   653    defeqC : HashMap.RelOn ExprPairWF st.defeq_c lst.defeqC absExprPair id
   654    annotC : HashMap.RelOn ExprWF st.annot_c lst.annotC absExpr absExpr
   655    lsimpC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lsimp_c lst.lsimpC absLevel absLevel
   656    lnzC : HashMap.RelOn LevelWF st.lnz_c lst.lnzC absLevel id
   657    eqvC : HashMap.RelOn LevelPairWF st.eqv_c lst.eqvC absLevelPair id
   658    instC : HashMap.RelOn InstKeyWF st.inst_c lst.instC absInstKey absExpr
   659    /-- The `instC` table's **entry count**, which the other thirteen clauses do
   660    not need: `StateRel` is a lookup agreement and a lookup agreement does not
   661    bound the Lean map's size.  `cached::state_c::inst_list_m` is the one
   662    operation that reads a count — the `instC` entry cap, `inst_c.len() <
   663    inst_c_cap_c` against `mp.size < instCCapC` (`StateC.lean:186-199`) — so
   664    without this clause the two sides can disagree about whether the table is
   665    full.  Task #61 folded it in (`Refine/StateC.lean` had it as a free-standing
   666    `InstCSize` hypothesis that nothing could discharge). -/
   667    instCSize : (HashMap.al_v st.inst_c).length = lst.instC.size
   668  
   669  /-- The port-side invariant of the fourteen tables: each is a well-formed
   670  `ron::HashMap` (task #16's `Inv`) holding only well-formed keys and — where the
   671  values are terms — only well-formed values. -/

    97    absEnv fe.env = lfe.env ∧

    99    HashMap.RelOn NameWF fe.idx lfe.idx absName absIdxEntry

   104    inv : HashMap.Inv name.Name.Insts.Con_ron_coreRonHashmapHashable fe.idx

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Abs.lean#L515-L529
   515  inductive ExprWF : expr.Expr → Prop where
   516    | bvar {i e} : expr.bvar i = ok e → ExprWF e
   517    | fvar {idx ty e} : ExprWF ty → expr.fvar idx ty = ok e → ExprWF e
   518    | sort {u e} : LevelWF u → expr.sort u = ok e → ExprWF e
   519    | mk_const {n us e} : NameWF n → LevelsWF us → expr.mk_const n us = ok e → ExprWF e
   520    | app {f a e} : ExprWF f → ExprWF a → expr.app f a = ok e → ExprWF e
   521    | lam {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   522        expr.lam ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   523    | forall_e {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   524        expr.forall_e ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   525    | let_e {ty v b e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF v → ExprWF b →
   526        expr.let_e ty v b = ok e → ExprWF e
   527    | lit {l e} : LiteralWF l → expr.lit l = ok e → ExprWF e
   528    | proj {s i x e} : NameWF s → ExprWF x → expr.proj s i x = ok e → ExprWF e
   529

   115      (g : ConLeche.FEnv → ConLeche.Cached.CheckCM β) : Prop :=

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=
